sections.html:
Pearl is a Rankin County city on the east bank of the Pearl River, directly across from Jackson, and it is the most populous city in the county. The 2020 census counted 27,115 residents, with 10,926 households and a median age of 36.1 years. The city covers about 25.6 square miles and borders Flowood, Brandon, Richland and Jackson. U.S. Highway 80 is the main commercial street, and Interstate 20, Interstate 55, U.S. 49 and Mississippi Highway 25 (Lakeland Drive) all serve the area.

Pearl has its own city hall, police, fire department and school district, even though many people think of it as part of greater Jackson. Permits, code questions and school boundaries run through the city, while the property tax bill comes from Rankin County.

The median household income is $61,695 and the median property value is $182,500. Those are citywide figures, so a three-bedroom ranch near Old Brandon Road and a house with deferred repairs will not sit at the same number. Much of the housing came with suburban growth out of Jackson in the 1960s, which means sellers often own houses whose roofs, foundations and systems have aged. When a problem makes a house hard to finance, a cash buyer who takes the property as is becomes a practical option.

Rankin County values and bills the property, and the tax is due by February 1 for the preceding assessment year. If February 1 lands on a weekend or holiday, payment the following Monday carries no penalty or interest.

Under the Mississippi Constitution a single-family, owner-occupied home is Class I and assessed at 10 percent of true value. Other real estate, including a rental house or an inherited home nobody lives in, is Class II at 15 percent. The bill equals true value times the assessment ratio times the combined millage of the county, city and school district. Assessors must revalue real property at least every four years.

The Tax Collector mails statements by December and takes payment at (601) 825-1467 or through the county's online payment page. Unpaid property goes to a tax sale in August, and the owner has two years from the sale date to redeem it before it passes to the buyer or the State. If you are behind, the balance has to be cleared before clean title can pass, so ask the Tax Collector for a payoff figure early.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption when a house sells
sections.html:
The exemption follows whoever lives in the home on January 1, so a sale changes who can claim it. A buyer must own and occupy the house as a primary residence on January 1 of the tax year, and the deed must be filed with the Chancery Clerk before January 7. Applications go to the county Tax Assessor between January 1 and April 1.

Homestead tierWho qualifiesBenefit
RegularOwners under 65Credit of up to $300
Age or disabilityOwners 65 or older, or totally disabledExempt on the first $7,500 of assessed value
Disabled service membersSome disabled former service members and surviving spousesFull exemption

A buyer who closes in spring probably cannot get the exemption for that year, and an investor who buys to rent never qualifies. A house sold by an owner who had the exemption may need a fresh application from the next owner. Sorting this out at the closing table avoids a surprise on the following tax bill.

sections.h2: What a Pearl seller must disclose
sections.html:
Mississippi requires most sellers to give the buyer a written property condition disclosure statement. Under Section 89-1-503 it must be delivered as soon as practicable before title transfers, and the seller notes compliance on the contract or an addendum.

If the statement arrives after the buyer has made an offer, the buyer has three days after hand delivery, or five days after mailing, to cancel the offer in writing. A buyer who gets a skipped or partly completed form is presumed to be on notice to ask about the missing items, and agents are not disciplined for the omission.

  • Fill in the form honestly, including known roof leaks, foundation movement and past water damage.
  • Keep receipts for repairs, since they answer most buyer questions.
  • Hand over the statement with the first offer rather than later, so no one gets a cancellation window.

A cash buyer who purchases as is still receives the disclosure. The difference is that the buyer prices in the repairs instead of asking you to make them.

sections.h2: Ways to sell fast in Pearl
sections.html:
A Pearl seller can list with an agent, sell directly to an investor for cash, or fix the house first and then list. The best choice depends on the condition of the house and how soon you need to close.

  • Listing suits a house in good shape and a seller who can wait through showings, inspections and a buyer's loan approval.
  • A direct cash sale suits houses with repair needs, tax or probate pressure, tenants, or a move on a deadline.
  • Repair-then-list can work if the repairs are cosmetic and cheap, but costs add up and take time.

New employers and road links may help neighborhood demand over time, but they do not fix a house that needs work today. Do not count on future projects to carry a listing.

Before any sale, a title search shows liens, unpaid taxes and whether the seller holds legal title. The Rankin County Chancery Clerk requires a deed with a notarized seller signature, a legal description with indexing instructions, and names, addresses and phone numbers for sellers, buyers and the preparer. Only an attorney or title company can search the records and draft the deed. If permit work was left open on the house, the City of Pearl's Community Development office on Old Brandon Road is the place to ask.

Cash Home Buyers works with Pearl sellers who want a straightforward as-is sale, and we explain what we can and cannot offer up front.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell my house in Pearl, MS?
faqs.a: It depends on the route. A cash sale can close as soon as the title work is ready, while a listing waits on showings, a buyer's loan and an appraisal. Title problems and unpaid taxes slow either path.

faqs.q: Do I need to make repairs before selling in Pearl?
faqs.a: No. Mississippi does not require repairs before a sale, but you must complete the written property condition disclosure statement. Buyers who purchase as is typically price the repairs in.

faqs.q: When are Rankin County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By February 1 for property assessed the preceding year. If that date falls on a weekend or holiday, you have until the following Monday without penalty.
The Pearl Public School District serves the city, and it has its own schools from lower elementary through Pearl High School.

faqs.q: Who records the deed when a Pearl house sells?
faqs.a: The Rankin County Chancery Clerk. The deed needs a notarized seller signature and a legal description, and a title company or attorney normally prepares it.
